solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Shell stuffed with fish and duck (7)

indicators.note: the shell is filled with the fish, so the fish goes inside

blocks.note: a pod is the shell of a pea or bean

annotation.surface: A seafood recipe: a pastry shell filled with fish and duck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' sits at the end looking like a second filling, but it is the definition; 'and' merely joins it to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain naming: the pochard is a species of diving duck, the males with a chestnut head.

entries.clue: With leader demoted, nation cheers royal with great care (13)

indicators.note: the first letter is moved down to the end of the word

blocks.note: SPAIN with its first letter S moved to the back

annotation.surface: A demoted leader watches the nation cheer a royal who treats everyone with great care.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Demoted' in a down clue means sent lower, so Spain's leading S drops to the bottom. TA is British informal for thanks, which is also what 'cheers' means.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taking pains over something is taking great care with it.

entries.clue: This French saint gets upset over collection of filth (7)

indicators.note: asks for the French word for 'this'
in a down clue, turned over means read upwards

blocks.note: TIPS (gets upset, as a boat tips) turned over

annotation.surface: A French saint is dismayed to find himself above a heap of filth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like distress, but here it is the physical sense: something that tips over is upset.
annotation.definitionFit: A cesspit is a pit where sewage and filth collect.

entries.clue: Collection artist mounted on beam (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going up, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: RA (Royal Academician, an artist) turned upwards
a ray is a beam of light

annotation.surface: A gallery collection: an artist's work mounted on a wooden beam.
annotation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist. 'On' tells you the artist sits above the beam in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: An array is an impressive collection or display of things.

entries.clue: Sport in city Den’s abandoned: wise man! (8)

indicators.note: DEN is left out of the city's name

blocks.note: a sage is a wise man

annotation.surface: Someone named Den has left the city to play sport, and a bystander praises his wisdom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Den' looks like a man's name (as in the soap EastEnders), but it is simply the letters to strip from Dresden, the German city.
annotation.definitionFit: Dressage is the equestrian sport of training a horse to perform precise movements.

entries.clue: Draw somersaulting relative next to ring (6)

indicators.note: a somersault turns the word head over heels, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a peal is a ring of bells

annotation.surface: A child draws a picture of a tumbling relative beside a ring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw' is a noun here, as in a big draw at the box office, not the verb for sketching.
annotation.definitionFit: A draw is something that attracts people, which is appeal.

entries.clue: Hard propping up area towards the rear (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, what props something up sits beneath it

annotation.surface: Something hard holds up an area at the back of a building.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay is written hard-first, but 'propping up' puts STERN below A in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word meaning towards or at the rear of a ship.

entries.clue: Part of gospel man is making test of memory (9)

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'gospel' through 'man is' into the first letter of 'making'

annotation.surface: A test of memory in which someone must recall a passage of the gospel.
annotation.walkthrough: Pelmanism is the card game also called pairs or pelmanism, where face-down cards are turned two at a time; it is named after the Pelman memory-training system.
annotation.definitionFit: Pelmanism is a memory game of matching pairs of face-down cards.

entries.clue: Charge city’s former university admissions body retrospectively (7)

indicators.note: looking back, so the whole string reads in reverse

blocks.note: LA'S: Los Angeles is the city
UCCA, the Universities Central Council on Admissions, since replaced by UCAS

annotation.surface: A city charges its former university admissions body after the fact.
annotation.walkthrough: UCCA was the British body handling university applications until 1993, when it merged into UCAS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an accusal, an old word for accusation, is a charge laid against someone.

entries.clue: Wearing end to attacks by earnest rebel (9)

indicators.note: take the last letter of the following word

blocks.note: wearing = in, as in dressed in

annotation.surface: A rebel grows weary of the attacks made by an earnest opponent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' reads as tiring, but it means in, as in someone in a hat.
annotation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel fighting against authority.

entries.clue: Cold decoy’s sucking lolly (5)

indicators.note: the decoy draws the letter in

blocks.note: a lure is a decoy; the 's is 'is'

annotation.surface: A child uses a cold ice lolly as bait.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lolly' looks like an ice lolly, but it is British slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially ill-gotten; lolly is British slang for money.

entries.clue: Poet is beneath hosting Society writers led by editor Mike (6,7)

indicators.note: UNDER holds the society and writers inside it
to be led by someone is to have them walking in front, so ED and M come first

blocks.note: Mike is M in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A poet feels beneath a society of writers whose meeting is chaired by an editor called Mike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is beneath' looks like part of the surface's grammar, but it is a single piece of wordplay, UNDER, split open to take the society of writers.
annotation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

entries.clue: Old soldier sure about crossing river (5)

indicators.note: 'about' as in about-turn: YES faces the other way and reads backwards
the reversed word lies across the river, holding it

annotation.surface: A veteran soldier is certain of his route across a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as concerning, but it turns YES back to front before PO goes in.
annotation.definitionFit: A sepoy was an Indian soldier serving under British or European command.

entries.clue: Plant in main island almost meeting fuel total (9)

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so it stops one letter short of the end

blocks.note: SARK, a Channel Island, without its last letter

annotation.surface: An island running low on fuel tallies the total cost of its main power plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the old poetic word for the open sea, so the definition is a sea plant. 'Plant' and 'fuel' together suggest a power station.
annotation.definitionFit: Sargassum is a brown seaweed that floats in great masses in the ocean, the main.

entries.clue: Relate funny turn for trusted friend (5,3)

indicators.note: strange, so the letters come out rearranged

annotation.surface: Telling a funny story is a way to make a trusted friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relate' looks like the verb for telling a story; it is simply six letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: An alter ego, literally other self, is a close and trusted friend.

entries.clue: Wealthy male curbing European seat of power (9)

indicators.note: RICH restrains E inside it

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer, or a man at a stag party

annotation.surface: A rich man keeps a European out of the seat of power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Curbing' sits between 'male' and 'European' as if the man is holding back the European, but it is the wealth that does the holding, with the male tacked on after.
annotation.definitionFit: The Reichstag in Berlin houses the German parliament.

entries.clue: Poorly splits bit of fish substitute (4-2)

indicators.note: ILL goes into FIN and parts it

blocks.note: a fin is part of a fish

annotation.surface: A sick cook botches the filleting of a fish.
annotation.walkthrough: Poorly is British for unwell, not badly.
annotation.definitionFit: A fill-in is a person or thing used as a substitute.

entries.clue: Item made by man at cafe traveller partly recalled (8)

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words before it
called back, so read backwards

blocks.note: the letters start at the T of 'at', run through 'cafe' and stop after TRA of 'traveller', then read right to left

annotation.surface: A souvenir made by a man at a café, which a traveller only half remembers.
annotation.walkthrough: Read backwards, T-CAFE-TRA gives ARTEFACT. The definition runs on into 'man at' so smoothly that the hiding place seems to start later than it does.
annotation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human hands.

entries.clue: Stalin’s police chief on centre of quiet peninsula (6)

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, the one standing in the middle
in an across clue, Beria goes after I

blocks.note: Lavrentiy Beria, head of Stalin's NKVD

annotation.surface: Stalin's secret police chief turns his attention to a quiet peninsula.
annotation.walkthrough: You need to know Lavrentiy Beria, Stalin's feared secret police chief.
annotation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula shared by Spain and Portugal.

entries.clue: Bird delayed rival successfully (7)

blocks.note: the emu, a large flightless bird

annotation.surface: A bird that got off to a late start still beat its rival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rival' is a verb here, as in to match.
annotation.definitionFit: To emulate is to match or equal someone, to rival them successfully.

entries.clue: Prudish character simpers dreadfully around knight (8)

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters hold N

annotation.surface: A prim woman simpers dreadfully when a knight is around.
annotation.walkthrough: In chess notation a knight is N, since K is taken by the king.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by quality: primness is the prudish character itself, a stiff and proper manner.

entries.clue: Bare Trojan hero on film out of position (7)

indicators.note: stripped of the outer letters

blocks.note: HECTOR without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A Trojan hero appears naked on film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bare' reads as naked, but it strips Hector of his outer letters. 'On' in a down clue puts ECTO above PIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Ectopic means occurring in an abnormal position, as in an ectopic pregnancy.

entries.clue: Saddo caught lifting antiseptic (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letters are raised so they read upwards

annotation.surface: A sad case gets caught lifting a bottle of antiseptic.
annotation.walkthrough: A saddo is British slang for a pathetic person. 'Lifting' looks like shoplifting, but it turns everything upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Cresol is a coal-tar compound used as an antiseptic and disinfectant.

entries.clue: Cowboy losing ring inside of herd: that is clumsiness (9)

indicators.note: the cowboy word drops the letter
the inside of a word is what lies within its outer letters, here the middle two

annotation.surface: A cowboy loses his lasso among the herd, which is clumsy of him.
annotation.walkthrough: A gaucho is a South American cowboy. 'Ring' looks like a lasso, but it is the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: Gaucherie is awkward, clumsy behaviour.

entries.clue: University class on religion that goes over bishop’s head (5)

blocks.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
RE = religious education, a school subject

annotation.surface: A university lecture on religion that is too difficult even for a bishop to follow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goes over bishop's head' suggests something beyond his understanding; the definition means it literally. RE is the British school subject religious education.
annotation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall headdress a bishop wears.

entries.clue: Second half of dance perhaps for Joe in LA (5)

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
half of the CHA-CHA, an example of a dance

annotation.surface: The second half of the dance is for someone called Joe who lives in Los Angeles.
annotation.walkthrough: Joe is American slang for coffee, so 'Joe in LA' is coffee in America. 'Perhaps' says the cha-cha is only one example of a dance.
annotation.definitionFit: Mocha is a kind of coffee, and joe is American slang for coffee.

entries.clue: Point on back of dry riser? (5)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so its final letter
in an across clue, EAST goes after Y

annotation.surface: A plumbing query about a dry riser, the pipe that carries water up a building.
annotation.walkthrough: A dry riser is a firefighting water pipe in a building; the question mark warns that 'riser' is used playfully, for what makes dough rise.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic nickname: yeast is the raising agent that makes dough rise, so it is playfully called a riser.

entries.clue: Pictures from envelopes turned heads (9)

indicators.note: turned round, so read backwards

blocks.note: a head is a headland, a cape

annotation.surface: Photographs fall out of envelopes, and heads turn to look.
annotation.walkthrough: An SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, sent so someone can reply. 'Heads' sounds like people looking, but it means headlands.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a seascape is one kind of picture, a painting or photograph of the sea.

entries.clue: Former province began to break up ending in downfall (6)

indicators.note: the letters of BEGAN come apart and rearrange
the ending of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: A former province of an empire began to break apart, ending in its collapse.
annotation.walkthrough: Bengal was a province of British India, split in 1947 between India and what became Bangladesh.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical label: Bengal was a province of British India, divided in 1947, so it is a former province.

entries.clue: Hit craft to the left circling key vehicle on track (7)

indicators.note: read leftwards, backwards
the reversed letters go round C

annotation.surface: A boat is struck while turning left around a key vehicle on the tracks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat that has been hit, but it means skill. The reversal applies to both words together, and only then does the key go inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a tram, a vehicle running on rails.
